sections.h2: If Arizona has no estate tax, what could heirs owe on an inherited house?
sections.html:
The tax questions for heirs in Arizona are federal estate tax on very large estates and income tax on any gain after a sale. The state guide above covers Arizona's own position. This section covers the pieces that still reach an heir who is trying to sell a house after a death.

Most Arizona families who inherit a house face paperwork rather than a tax bill: who has authority to sign, whether a court must be involved, and how creditors are handled. Each of those has a statute behind it, and each can slow a sale if it is skipped.

sections.h2: When does federal estate tax apply to an estate that includes an Arizona house?
sections.html:
Federal estate tax applies only when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, exceeds the filing threshold for the year of death. The IRS estate tax page says most simple estates do not need to file a return.

The IRS lists these filing thresholds by year of death:

Year of deathFiling threshold
2022$12,060,000
2023$12,920,000
2024$13,610,000
2025$13,990,000
2026$15,000,000

The IRS also notes that estates of decedents survived by a spouse may elect to pass along unused exemption on a timely filed estate tax return. The value used is fair market value at the date of death, not what the owner paid. That date-of-death value for the house is worth documenting even when no return is due.

sections.h2: Who can sell an inherited house in Arizona right after a death?
sections.html:
Only someone with legal authority can sign a deed, and in Arizona that is usually a court-appointed personal representative, a successor who has used a statutory affidavit, or a beneficiary named in a recorded beneficiary deed. Which path applies depends on how the owner held title.

Under A.R.S. 14-3715, a personal representative acting reasonably for the benefit of interested persons may sell, mortgage or lease estate real property for cash or credit, unless the will or a court order limits that power. The same statute lets the representative make repairs, insure the assets, and pay taxes and administration expenses from the estate.

If the personal representative has not yet been appointed, a buyer or an escrow officer will not close, because nobody can yet deliver good title.

sections.h2: Can heirs skip probate with an affidavit of succession?
sections.html:
Sometimes. A.R.S. 14-3971 lets successors file an affidavit for real property when the estate is small enough, and the statute sets specific conditions.

  • At least six months must have passed since the death, shown by a certified death certificate attached to the affidavit.
  • No application for a personal representative may be pending, and none may have been appointed, with real property in the estate valued at $300,000 or less after liens and encumbrances.
  • That value is taken from the full cash value on the assessment rolls for the year of death.
  • Funeral expenses, last illness expenses and all unsecured debts must be paid.
  • The signers must be entitled to the property as heirs or devisees, with no one else holding a right to it.
  • No federal estate tax may be due.

The affidavit is filed in the court of the county where the person lived, a certified copy is issued, and that copy is recorded with the county recorder where the house sits. The normal court filing fee applies unless it is waived.

A separate affidavit in the same statute covers personal property up to $200,000 after 30 days, which can help clear out a vehicle or accounts, but it does not replace the real property affidavit.

sections.h2: What if the owner recorded a beneficiary deed?
sections.html:
A recorded beneficiary deed can move title to the named person at the owner's death without probate. A.R.S. 33-405 says the deed must state that it is effective on the death of the owner and must be executed and recorded with the county recorder in the county where the property lies before the owner dies.

Points that come up for heirs:

  • The transfer is subject to mortgages, liens and other encumbrances the owner had at death.
  • An owner may revoke the deed any time before death by recording a revocation.
  • If more than one beneficiary deed is recorded, the last one recorded before death controls.
  • A beneficiary deed is not revoked by a later will.
  • If no named grantee survives the owner and no successor beneficiary is named, the deed is void.

The statute does not require the grantee beneficiary to sign or be told while the owner is alive, so some heirs learn of the deed only after the death. Check the county recorder's records early.

sections.h2: How long can heirs wait before opening an estate?
sections.html:
Arizona sets an outside limit of two years after death for opening most probate proceedings. A.R.S. 14-3108 says an informal probate or appointment, or a formal testacy or appointment proceeding, may not start more than two years after the death, with listed exceptions.

One exception allows a later proceeding if no court proceeding about the succession or administration has occurred within the two years. In that case the personal representative has no right to hold estate assets beyond what is needed to confirm title with the rightful successors, and claims other than expenses of administration cannot be presented.

Where there is no administration at all, A.R.S. 14-3901 says heirs and devisees take under the probated will or the laws of intestacy, subject to charges incident to administration, creditor claims and allowances to a surviving spouse and dependent children.

sections.h2: How do creditor claims affect the sale of an Arizona house from an estate?
sections.html:
Creditor claims can follow the house into the hands of heirs, so they are worth settling before or at closing. Under A.R.S. 14-3803, claims that arose before death are barred unless presented within the earlier of two years after death plus any notice period, or the time set by the statute for creditors who receive actual notice or publication.

The same statute says claims arising at or after death, including contract claims against the personal representative, are barred unless presented within four months after performance is due or after the claim arises, with the two-year rule applying for the later date on other claims. Enforcement of a mortgage or other lien on estate property is not affected by these limits, which is why a lender can still pursue the house itself.

sections.h2: What does the county recorder need at closing of an inherited house?
sections.html:
The recorder needs the deed and a completed affidavit of legal value. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires the seller and buyer, or their agents, to certify details such as names and addresses, the legal description, the date of sale, the total consideration, the type of financing and the assessor's parcel number.

The affidavit also asks whether a house will be owner-occupied or rented and whether the parties are related. The recorder must refuse to record without a complete affidavit unless the instrument bears a listed exemption.

An estate sale also needs whatever proves the seller's authority, such as letters from the court or the recorded affidavit of succession. The title company will tell you which documents it needs.

sections.h2: What are common problems for sellers of inherited Arizona houses?
sections.html:
The most common problems are missing authority, unpaid debts, and a house that has sat vacant. These are practical points, not tax rules, but each one affects how fast a sale can close.

  • No personal representative appointed, so no one can sign.
  • Heirs who live in different states and must all agree.
  • A mortgage or lien that survives the death and must be paid from the sale.
  • Back taxes or repairs that have piled up while the house sat empty.
  • Uncertainty about the value for date-of-death purposes.

A cash buyer can purchase a house as it stands, which removes repair work from the to-do list. The legal steps above still apply to the title.

faqs.q: Does Arizona charge an estate tax or inheritance tax?
faqs.a: The guide above states that Arizona repealed its estate tax and does not impose an inheritance or gift tax. Federal estate tax is a separate matter and applies only above the IRS filing threshold, which is $15,000,000 for a death in 2026.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Arizona house without probate?
faqs.a: Yes, if you hold title through a recorded beneficiary deed or you qualify to file an affidavit of succession for real property valued at $300,000 or less after liens, with at least six months passed since the death. Otherwise a court-appointed personal representative must sign.

faqs.q: How long do I have to open probate in Arizona?
faqs.a: The outside limit is generally two years after the death for most informal and formal proceedings, with exceptions listed in A.R.S. 14-3108.

faqs.q: Can a personal representative sell the house?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the will or a court order restricts it. A.R.S. 14-3715 lets a personal representative sell, mortgage or lease estate real property for cash or credit, acting reasonably for the interested persons.

faqs.q: What affidavit does the county recorder require for the sale?
faqs.a: An affidavit of legal value must be attached to the deed at recording. It states the parties, legal description, date of sale, total consideration and type of financing.
